Color analysis (also called seasonal color analysis or personal color analysis) is a method of finding the specific colors that look best on you based on your natural coloring — skin tone, eye color, and hair color. It categorizes people into 'seasons' (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter) with sub-types for more precision, each with its own recommended color palette.

Color analysis is based on color theory principles — specifically how different colors interact with your skin's undertone, creating either harmonious or clashing visual effects. While it's not 'hard science,' the underlying principles of color harmony and contrast are well-established in art, design, and optics.

Color analysis isn't just for women. Knowing your best colors can transform your professional image, simplify shopping, and ensure every suit, shirt, and casual outfit works with your natural coloring. Men who understand their color season make better wardrobe investments and always look polished.

Colors that clash with your specific undertone

Colors that clash with your undertone bring out unflattering yellow or gray tones in your skin. If warm colors make you look yellowish, you're likely cool-toned. If cool colors make you look washed out, you're likely warm-toned.

Colors that clash with your undertone emphasize the 'wrong' pigments in your skin. If you're cool-toned, warm colors like orange or mustard can make your skin look yellowish. If you're warm-toned, cool colors like icy pink or silver can bring out redness.

Cool Summer, also called True Summer, is the purest expression of the Summer season. These individuals have distinctly cool undertones with medium depth and moderate contrast. Their coloring has a noticeable coolness — skin with blue or pink undertones, ashy hair, and cool-toned eyes. Cool Summers are most flattered by medium-depth cool colors that are neither too light nor too dark.
Cool Winter — distinctly cool undertones with dark coloring

Cool Winter, also called True Winter, is the purest expression of the Winter season. These individuals have distinctly cool undertones with medium-to-high contrast and clear, bold coloring. There is no warmth in their coloring — everything reads cool, from their skin (often with blue or pink undertones) to their hair and eyes. Cool Winters look best in pure, cool, and saturated colors with no warmth.
